mechanisms: vertical balance and center-of-gravity placement can change a kawaii rating without defining one mandatory cute pose
a pose impression emerges from posture category performer variation and viewer judgment rather than one limb angle

a still image needs a visible support foot contact point or shared task anchor to make the intended balance and relationship legible
adult status comes from explicit subject declaration plus adult work or life context and is never inferred from body proportions

photographic_evidence_definitions.pose_vertical_balance_cue: The standing or seated silhouette has a clearly readable vertical balance line and supported base.
photographic_evidence_definitions.pose_weight_shift_action: Hip shoulder and support-foot alignment visibly show weight transferred toward or away from the current task.
photographic_evidence_definitions.gesture_inward_compaction: One restrained inward elbow hand or shoulder gesture is visible without compressing every limb into an infantilized pose.
photographic_evidence_definitions.dyad_interpersonal_distance_band: The relative gap between adult subjects is visibly framed together with the scene constraint that permits it.
photographic_evidence_definitions.dyad_mutual_orientation_blocking: Both torsos or head directions visibly converge toward each other or the shared task.
photographic_evidence_definitions.dyad_shared_gaze_target: Both subjects visibly attend to the same object work surface or event.
photographic_evidence_definitions.dyad_compensatory_lean: One subject visibly leans or turns while the other maintains distance, making the spatial adjustment legible.
photographic_evidence_definitions.functional_reach_task_anchor: A handoff object tool work surface or obstacle visibly explains the subjects' reach and spacing.

compatibility_rules: combine a compact gesture with stable balance and one readable support point
combine closer dyad spacing with mutual orientation or a shared target when affiliation or cooperation is intended
combine an asymmetric lean with a visible handoff or task object when tentative approach is intended
combine wider spacing with convergent gaze or parallel action when emotional connection should remain readable at a distance
conflict_rules: do not prescribe a universal intimacy meaning from an exact centimeter distance
do not combine incompatible balance states such as a deep forward transfer and rigidly centered weight without a supporting action
do not stack every inward hand foot head and shoulder gesture into one infantilized silhouette
do not claim affection from close spacing when crowding task geometry or camera compression provides a simpler explanation
counterexamples: crossed arms can stabilize posture or protect from cold rather than signal hostility
close proximity in a narrow location does not by itself indicate intimacy
inward feet or lowered shoulders do not universally mean cuteness or shyness
a low center of gravity can be a work stance or athletic preparation rather than an emotional display
boundaries: explicit_adult_subject_declaration and adult_work_or_life_context are required; body proportions never prove chronological age
no pose distance gaze pattern gender or cultural group is treated as a personality determinant
accessibility aids seated balance and restricted movement remain valid expressive configurations
distance is rendered relative to the shared action and framing rather than as a universal cultural measurement
no named character pose signature gesture or franchise staging is reproduced
cute impression remains a viewer-dependent target and never evidence of chronological age

ja.かわいい: The primary study treats kawaii as a rated affective impression influenced by posture, not as one fixed body configuration.
ja.対人距離: The Japanese proxemics study examines interpersonal-distance change together with gaze head and body orientation lean and other behavior; the term does not license a universal distance-emotion lookup.

mechanisms: a conventional manga mark can modify the reading of a neutral face for viewers familiar with that visual language

compatibility_rules: pair one facial or gestural anchor with at most one environmental translation cue
use directional background rhythm only when an actual movement or gaze direction supports it
pair a practical blush-color cue with gaze aversion hand placement or another visible social action
use prop geometry or focus disruption for uncertainty only when the scene contains a decision target
conflict_rules: do not place literal emoji readable text proprietary UI or floating manga glyphs into a photographic-realism route
do not stack several symbols that imply incompatible arousal direction or scene functions
do not let an environmental cue replace all facial bodily and action evidence
do not treat a culturally learned symbol as universally decoded
counterexamples: visible perspiration can indicate heat or exertion rather than embarrassment
cheek color can come from temperature lighting or makeup rather than affection
red or hard lighting does not inherently mean anger
circular bokeh or a tilted prop does not independently prove confusion
boundaries: no named IP panel composition signature symbol placement character palette or catchphrase is reproduced
no real social-platform UI logo notification or readable message is used as an emotion shortcut
no enlarged eyes deformed anatomy or age-regressive facial proportions are required for the live-action translation
translated cues are not used to diagnose a mental neurological or medical state
adult subjects are explicitly declared and nonsexualized styling remains the default
practical translations are design inferences rather than claims that the cited studies tested those photographic effects

place wear at plausible cuffs knees elbows hems closures load points or tool-contact areas for the chosen material and action

corroborate occupational clothing with an observable task or location rather than a label alone
conflict_rules: do not describe long hard use while rendering every fabric surface factory-pristine without an explicit replacement reason
do not distribute identical dirt tears or fading evenly across unrelated materials and contact zones
do not keep every formal closure and accessory in a relaxed off-duty state unless the scene gives a reason
do not infer temperament morality competence or class worth from a garment category
counterexamples: a uniform does not establish whether a character is strict warm shy or rebellious
an open collar can reflect heat fit a break period or rushed action rather than carelessness
a stain does not by itself imply poverty low status or poor hygiene
a visible repair may indicate care necessity resourcefulness fashion or institutional maintenance
boundaries: adult subjects are explicitly declared and youth-coded school uniforms are never combined with sexualized styling
no real police military medical school employer insignia credential or rank mark is reproduced
no class gender ethnicity nationality or occupation is assigned a fixed personality through clothing
damage and aging remain physically plausible for the depicted textile and action
continuity state is not treated as reliable chronology without scene context
no named IP silhouette signature palette costume accessory or transformation outfit is copied

frequent contact can be job necessity rather than emotional attachment
damage can result from one accident rather than a long relationship
